articles.title: Sony is shutting down its live TV service PlayStation Vue in January 2020
articles.summary: Sony is shutting down its live TV streaming service PlayStation Vue on January 30th, 2020, the company announced today. The sudden announcement of the shutdown comes just a week after a report published by The Information saying Sony was looking for a buyer for the service, which has continually lost money for the company since its launch in March of 2015.
articles.body: Sony is shutting down its live TV streaming service PlayStation Vue on January 30th, 2020, the company announced today. The sudden announcement of the shutdown comes just a week after a report published by The Information saying Sony was looking for a buyer for the service, which has continually lost money for the company since its launch in March of 2015. Sony has repeatedly raised the price of Vue to try to offset its rising costs, most recently by $5 across all plans back in July. “Unfortunately, the highly competitive Pay TV industry, with expensive content and network deals, has been slower to change than we expected. Because of this, we have decided to remain focused on our core gaming business,” Sony said in a blog post announcing the shutdown. “PlayStation fans can continue to access movie and TV content through the PlayStation Store on PS4 and via our partnerships with top entertainment apps.” PlayStation Vue launched four years ago as an early competitor in the so-called pay-TV market, which is a restructured form of cable made popular by companies like Sling. Like most other vendors, Sony offered a skinny bundle of channels with the option to add more premium ones, like sports and entertainment channels, by paying a higher monthly subscription fee. After the price hike, the entry-level Vue plan cost about $50 a month. At its height, Vue amassed about 500,000 subscribers, which is far less than competitors like Sling and YouTube TV, The Information reported last week. Ultimately, it looks like Sony couldn’t make the economics work, as the cost of licensing cable channels far outweighed the money Sony could recoup on subscriptions. Vue’s demise is also a signal that customer interest in traditional cable bundles, skinny or otherwise, continues to shrink. As a result, major players in the entertainment industry are throwing immense resources toward building out proper, on-demand streaming services to compete with Amazon and Netflix. That includes Disney with Disney+, Apple with Apple TV Plus, AT&T with HBO Max, and NBCUniversal with Peacock, among others.

articles.title: Hollywood is bending the knee to OpenAI
articles.summary: Studios’ reluctance to acquire Luca Guadagnino’s Artificial is a troubling sign for the entertainment industry.﻿
articles.body: Netflix, A24, Focus Features, and Warner Bros.’ Clockwork have all reportedly decided to pass on picking up Artificial — director Luca Guadagnino’s new biographical drama about OpenAI cofounder / CEO Sam Altman — for distribution deals. And while Neon and Mubi are still said to be interested in the film, this situation makes it seem like Hollywood no longer has the courage to tell critical stories about Big Tech. Postproduction on Artificial was nearly finished when Amazon MGM unexpectedly announced last week that it no longer plans to distribute the film. The news came as a surprise given how far along the movie was and reports that Amazon initially intended to give it a short, Oscar-qualifying theatrical run some time later this year. Artificial was also reportedly scheduled for a wider release in early 2027 and a showing at the SXSW Film & TV Festival, but those plans are now dead in the water. Though Amazon hasn’t gone into detail about why it dropped Artificial, the company told Deadline that it felt the film would be “better served if it were released by a different studio.” While Neon or Mubi could ultimately be better homes for the project, Amazon’s decision follows its $50 billion investment into OpenAI from earlier this year. Amazon has made abundantly clear that it wants to be in the AI business in a big way, and it’s easy to understand why the company might be reluctant to release a film that portrays an AI executive in a negative light. But the larger issue is the fact that Amazon probably won’t be the last studio to move this way. Written by An American Pickle scribe Simon Rich, Artificial chronicles the tumultuous period in 2023 when Altman was fired from OpenAI and subsequently rehired just a few days later. The drama began with OpenAI’s board of directors alleging that Altman was hindering “its ability to exercise its responsibilities” by not being “consistently candid in his communications” (corporate PR speak for “lying.”) Shortly after, Altman was set to join Microsoft and hundreds of OpenAI employees signed an open letter threatening to quit if he wasn’t reinstated as CEO. Things concluded with Altman returning to OpenAI and installing a fresh board of directors almost entirely full of new faces. On paper at least, the entire saga reads like a drama that could make for a gripping and timely examination of one of Silicon Valley’s most powerful executives. After projects like The Audacity, Mountainhead, The Dropout, and Aaron Sorkin’s forthcoming The Social Reckoning, Artificial feels like the sort of film that aligns with Hollywood’s recent fixation on stories about tech titans. And in this era of generative AI being shoved down everyone’s throats, audiences are primed for a star-studded feature focused on some of the people responsible for the technology’s omnipresence. What’s truly alarming, though, is how many other studios have chosen to follow Amazon’s lead. Yesterday, Google’s DeepMind AI arm announced that it has struck a $75 million, multiyear “research partnership” deal with A24 to develop a host of filmmaking technologies like a new storyboarding application. The companies have said that the deal won’t involve Google gaining access to A24’s library of film and TV projects, but they have yet to make clear the extent to which these tools will be used by the studio. That lack of clarity is part of why people have already begun to take a dimmer view of A24. Just last week, the studio was riding high on the breakout success of Backrooms, but after posting the trailer for Jesse Eisenberg’s upcoming musical The Debut, A24 has been met with a wave of scathing online criticism specifically because of the DeepMind collaboration. The chances of A24 and Google’s partnership dissolving feel unlikely because the production company is far from the only studio that has decided to get into bed with gen AI. Disney has struck (failed) AI deals of its own, Netflix has absorbed AI startups, and Paramount Skydance executives have signaled that they see the technology as being key to boosting productivity. All of this paints a very bleak picture of Hollywood’s possible future — one in which movies and series are produced with gen AI by studios that refuse to say anything truly insightful or negative about the technology or its creators. Projects like The AI Doc: Or How I Became an Apocaloptimist have already shown us how uninspired and soulless films about AI can be when they’re crafted by people who seem beholden to tech executives. And what we’re looking at now is a potential age of Hollywood giants doing everything in their power to stay in Silicon Valley’s good graces. Operating that way — from a place of cowardice in service of tech-driven profits — is antithetical to producing good art.

articles.title: Miley Cyrus drops last name ahead of new music release
articles.summary: The singer is embarking on a new era following the death of her beloved godmother, Dolly Parton.
articles.body:
Miley Cyrus mysteriously dropped her last name from her social media handles on Monday — and is now simply going by "Miley."

The singer did not provide her followers with any explanation for the move just yet. However, she did post two new red and black photos of herself via Instagram , pointedly captioning one of them, "MILEY."

It appears Cyrus, 33, is marking a new era after signing to Atlantic Records last month. She was previously with Sony Music's Columbia, as well as RCA.

She has yet to announce when she's dropping her highly anticipated 10th studio album, which would mark the followup to 2025's "Something Beautiful," released last May.

Cyrus did, however, talk about her new music in a Q&A for Wonderland magazine with actress Daryl Hannah last month.

"This album is a love story, but love stories are never one-dimensional. They're always layered," she shared at the time. "There is definitely a romantic thread weaving through it because, like all my records, it's a reflection of where I am in my life. But this one feels especially meaningful because this feeling has stayed with me through multiple eras."

She added, "That's something I hadn't really experienced before. A peaceful kind of love has become a theme across my last three records. Not just the love I share with someone else, but the love I've found form myself."

The "Wrecking Ball" singer, whose been engaged to producer Maxx Morando since December 2025, said she went through an "evolution."

"Once your relationship with yourself changes, every relationship around you changes too," she noted. "I think this record celebrates both of those equally."

The Grammy-winning singer was photographed last Tuesday heading into a Los Angeles studio to film an upcoming project in pics obtained by Page Six. Dressed in all black, she looked somber as news that her godmother , Dolly Parton, had died broke just hours earlier.

The "Hannah Montana" alum shared an emotional Instagram tribute to the country music icon, who died at 80 years old after a brief battle with cancer .

"I have an angel by my side. I always have. One of our last conversations was about music and metamorphosis.

"I will always love her and want to make her proud. My heart breaks for the world, her family and friends who will miss her deeply. We're in this loss together and we will see her in all of the most beautiful things."

articles.title: I went to the loneliest baseball game on Apple Vision Pro
articles.summary: For the first time, a Major League Baseball game between the Red Sox and Yankees was broadcast live on Apple Vision Pro. The tech is impressive, but who is it for?
articles.body: This weekend, I strapped on an Apple Vision Pro to watch a baseball game in immersive virtual reality for the first time. It was technically impressive, visually pretty remarkable, and also didn’t make that much sense. Apple and Major League Baseball chose a classic match-up of the Boston Red Sox and the New York Yankees for the first of its series of four games streamed on the device. I do not review tech for The Verge, but I do watch a lot of baseball — if there’s a game on and I’m at home, it’s likely on my television. If this is the future of sports, live events, and wearable technology in general, I’d like to see what all the fuss is about. The first thing to know about baseball is that it is long: in season, in game time, and in the arc of history. Right off the bat, this reality makes having a screen strapped to your face a hard sell. It’s not just the physical burden — like many others, I find the Vision Pro heavy and cumbersome — but also because it’s a time-honored tradition to get up and go do something else for a moment while the game is on. It’s America’s pastime for a reason: the slowness, the buildup, the culmination of a long, sticky season where teams slump and get hot. Some nights are duds and others are classics; you are playing (and watching) the long game. Even at the ballpark, you might get up to grab food or another beer, and the seventh inning stretch is built right into live play to give fans a break. With an immersive environment, I struggled with whiplash; coming in and out of the headset’s reality, going from zero to one hundred and back again anytime I wanted to grab a drink, walk around, or eat dinner. That said, the first time I put on the Vision Pro to watch the pregame show, I screamed — it’s surreal to see the players so close, from a new, intimate angle and proximity. It was arresting, surprising, and a little scary. As Yankees starting pitcher Cam Schlittler was warming up in the bullpen, all I could think was, “He really is so tall.” A pregame interview with Jazz Chisholm Jr. made me feel like I was standing uncomfortably close to him. The broadcast on Apple Vision Pro was clearly tailored to an audience who might not be as familiar with MLB or baseball in general: There was a lot of explaining how to watch the game, and many shoutouts to the Vision Pro viewers, of course. [Media: The feeling of being terrifyingly close didn’t last very long, though. On Vision Pro, you watch the game primarily from two angles, next to each team’s dugout when that team is batting (you’re stuck there, you don’t get to move around as you please). I liked this angle for certain batters, because you can see the vertical movement of pitches come in without anything blocking them. But for say, a righty batter whose team is watching from the third base dugout (or a lefty whose team is watching from the first base side), their body partially obstructs the view. The immersive view also doesn’t track the action in the outfield — your perspective is frozen next to the dugout. As a result, I felt both in the thick of it and at a strange remove; even ground balls and infield plays feel a bit far away, especially if you’re watching from the third base side and there’s traffic on first and second base. The immersive broadcast includes a floating jumbotron-style screen that shows a more traditional TV broadcast, along with player stats. I often found my attention drifting up to the standard broadcast, because once the ball leaves the vicinity of the batter, it’s quite hard to track what’s actually going on. The immersive replays from new vantage points like the outfield or closer to first base helped to bridge the feeling of being at a distance. But the Vision Pro’s view isn’t very reactive to what’s happening in real time. When Red Sox second baseman Nick Sogard hit a fly ball early in the game, it almost was a home run — but the immersive view was not very compelling. Baseball is full of weird moments, and it made me wonder how well those would be captured on the Vision Pro. What would the benches clearing in a heated moment look like, given the dugout is blacked out during innings? (For this iconic Red Sox-Yankees brawl, the dugout angle might actually be perfect.) How well could you follow the extremely rare and weird occurrences — like a ball getting wedged between the padding of a wall and the ground — that randomly become extremely important and that most people have never seen happen before? The Red Sox fly ball was caught up against the wall by Yankees centerfielder Trent Grisham in a hopping catch, but the immersive view alone wouldn’t be enough to follow the play closely. You need the TV broadcast screen to supplement the hyperreality. There were a few moments that really did feel like a new way to experience a very old game. The brief look into the team dugouts, for example, offered views you don’t often get: the screens tucked away with a live feed of the bullpens, or the sunflower seeds flying into the dirt. The on-deck circle, where players do their ritual preparations before it’s their turn up to bat, is visible only occasionally on a broadcast but is in full view on the Vision Pro. After Schlittler was pulled from the game in the sixth inning, the immersive view showed him in the dugout, shaking his head in frustration and heading into the clubhouse, head in hands. You probably wouldn’t get these details in a typical broadcast, at least not up close like this. On Saturday, I had a game on the TV while I made dinner for a friend, and on Sunday, a group of us caught the last Red Sox-Yankees game, live at Yankee Stadium, where the Yankees crushed the Sox 16-1. It all made me wonder who or what watching a game on Vision Pro is for. It’s remarkable technology that felt weirdly sterile and isolating as I sat on my couch, my friends watching me watch something alone. All of the most memorable baseball-related moments I’ve experienced happened in the company of others, and none of them depended on how good my view was or how close I was to the players. Immersive viewing might be a fun way for a casual fan or a techy person to engage with the game in a low stakes, convenient way. But if baseball is part of the rhythm of your day, or your summer, or your year, it’s hard to imagine regularly choosing the headset over just about any other way to follow the sport. I’d venture that for many baseball fans, the Vision Pro experience optimizes for the wrong thing. It’s novel and undoubtedly exciting — at least until you realize this isn’t what you came for to begin with.

articles.title: Man dies near Notting Hill Carnival after entering canal
articles.summary: The man was taken to hospital by ambulance and was pronounced dead a short time later, police have said.
articles.body:
A man died near Notting Hill Carnival in London on Monday afternoon, the Metropolitan Police have confirmed.

Police officers had attempted to stop the man, believed to be in his 20s, as he approached the event. He fled on foot with officers in pursuit, and entered the water in the vicinity of Meanwhile Gardens a short time later, the force said.

Taken to hospital by ambulance the man was pronounced dead a short time later.

Cdr Claire Smart said: "This is a tragic incident and our thoughts are with the loved ones of the man who has lost his life."

The Met Police said officers had attempted to stop the man at about 15:19 BST near Harrow Road.

The man entered the water in the vicinity of Meanwhile Gardens, off Kensal Road.

Officers and members of the public went in after him and pulled him from the water, police said, and officers immediately started CPR.

Paramedics were called and continued treatment at the canal side before taking the man to a central London hospital. He was pronounced dead at 16:43.

The Met Police said on Monday night that urgent enquiries were ongoing to locate and inform his next of kin.

Smart, gold commander for the Notting Hill Festival, said: "Any death following contact with the police is passed to the Independent Office for Police Conduct so the circumstances can be fully investigated.

"I would encourage everyone to avoid speculation while this work takes place."

She added: "I acknowledge the efforts of the officers and members of the public who entered the canal to rescue this man. I know they will be devastated that his life couldn't ultimately be saved."

The Met Police said the two days of the festival had passed "largely without incident".

There were two assaults with knives - one stabbing and one slashing. Neither resulted in life-threatening injuries.

On Monday evening, police said there had been 315 arrests that day, bringing the total number of arrests to 560.

articles.title: Djavan relança primeiro álbum, feito há 50 anos, em edição remixada que traz versões inéditas de faixas do LP de 1976 | G1
articles.body:
Djavan em foto da capa do álbum 'A voz • O violão • A música de Djavan', lançado em 1976 — Foto: Francisco Pereira / Reprodução da capa do álbum 'A voz • O violão • A música de Djavan'

♬ Lançado em 1976 pela gravadora Som Livre, o primeiro álbum de Djavan , “A voz • O violão • A música de Djavan” , ganha edição comemorativa de 50 anos em sincronia com o show da turnê com a qual o artista percorre o Brasil ao longo deste anos 2026 para celebrar cinco décadas de sucesso.

Nessa edição especial, prevista para chegar aos aplicativos na sexta-feira, 4 de setembro, o “A voz • O violão • A música de Djavan” volta com novas mixagem e masterização a cargo de Alexandre Rabaço e Max Viana.

Dois sambas do repertório autoral do álbum, “Embola a bola (Cateretê)” e “Muito obrigado”, reaparecem em registros inéditos de voz e violão, sem os toques dos músicos Altamiro Carrilho (1924 – 2012) (flauta), Hélio Delmiro (1947 – 2025) (guitarra), Luizão Maia (1949 – 2005) (baixo), Mestre Marçal (1930 – 1994) (percussão) e Paulo Braga (bateria). Já o samba “Maria das Mercedes” poderá ser ouvido em versão estendida.

Gravado no Estúdio Level, no Rio de Janeiro (RJ), com arranjos do tecladista Edson Frederico (1948 – 2011), o álbum “A voz • O violão • A música de Djavan” foi formatado com produção musical de Aloysio de Oliveira (1914 – 1995), sob direção de produção de Guto Graça Mello (1948 – 2026).

articles.title: Paloma Pitaya traduz ritmos nacionais e argentinos para a linguagem do violino no álbum autoral 'Caprichoso Brasil' | G1
articles.body:
Capa do álbum 'Caprichoso Brasil', da violonista e compositora Paloma Pitaya — Foto: Estúdio Thiago Drummond / Divulgação

♬ A arte tropical da capa do primeiro álbum autoral da compositora e violinista Paloma Pitaya, “Caprichoso Brasil”, evoca brasilidade que aparece mixada com toque erudito no álbum agendado para 25 de setembro.

É que Pitaya – instrumentista de formação erudita e atuação na área de pesquisa das tradições musicais latino-americanas – alinha no álbum 13 temas autorais de inspiração geralmente brasileira, todos compostos para o violino.

Nada menos do que 15 músicos tocam no álbum, como convidados de Paloma Pitaya, mas o mote de “Caprichoso Brasil” é o violino e eventualmente a rabeca, instrumento também tocado por essa musicista e compositora formada na Academia de Música da Osesp, onde estudou entre 2021 e 2023.

Entre outras atividades fora do Brasil, Pitaya foi compositora residente da Fundación Antonio Gala, na Espanha, onde teve a ideia do álbum “Caprichoso Brasil”. A propósito, o álbum se origina do livro de partituras para violino solo também intitulado “Caprichoso Brasil”, concebido pela artista entre 2019 e 2020 durante a residência artística na fundação espanhola e publicado neste ano de 2026.

No álbum, Paloma Pitaya expande o universo musical do livro ao harmonizar o violino e a rabeca com percussão, violão, sanfona, baixo elétrico e quarteto de cordas com arranjos que transitam entre o rigor da música de concerto e a pulsação vivaz das tradições populares.

Cada um dos 13 temas do álbum “Caprichoso Brasil” é batizado como “Capricho” seguido do nome do gênero musical. Os ritmos, em grande maioria, são brasileiros, como sinalizam temas como “Capricho baião”, “Capricho frevo”, “Capricho maxixe”, “Capricho samba” e “Capricho xote”. Contudo, a violinista também incursiona pela chacarera – ritmo argentino de origem rural – e a milonga, gênero que transita entre Argentina, Uruguai e o estado do Rio Grande do Sul.

Ao produzir o álbum “Caprichoso Brasil”, a intenção da instrumentista foi investigar como esses gêneros musicais podem ser reinterpretados por uma compositora de formação erudita e traduzidos para a linguagem do violino.

articles.title: Rock in Rio: 1º fim de semana tem previsão de chuva sábado e domingo | G1
articles.standfirst: Previsão indica máxima de 30°C na sexta e apenas 19°C no domingo; festival terá shows de Foo Fighters, Avenged Sevenfold, Calvin Harris e Elton John.
articles.summary: Previsão indica máxima de 30°C na sexta e apenas 19°C no domingo; festival terá shows de Foo Fighters, Avenged Sevenfold, Calvin Harris e Elton John.
articles.body:
Projeto do Palco Mundo do Rock in Rio 2022 — Foto: Divulgação

O primeiro fim de semana do Rock in Rio 2026 deve ser marcado por uma mudança brusca no tempo no Rio de Janeiro . Segundo a previsão do Climatempo, a sexta-feira (4), primeiro dia do festival, será de sol e máxima de 30°C , mas a chuva deve aparecer no sábado (5) e ganhar força no domingo (6), quando a temperatura não deve passar de 19°C.

A previsão aponta 85% de chance de chuva no sábado , com acumulado estimado de 7,2 milímetros, e 84% no domingo, quando são esperados 16,8 milímetros .

Na segunda-feira (7), feriado da Independência do Brasil, a temperatura continua baixa, com máxima de 19°C e possibilidade de chuva passageira durante o dia.

O cenário é especialmente importante para quem pretende passar várias horas na Cidade do Rock. O festival acontece no Parque Olímpico, na Barra da Tijuca, e reúne atrações em diferentes palcos ao longo de cada dia.

O Rock in Rio 2026 será realizado nos dias 4, 5, 6, 7, 11, 12 e 13 de setembro . No primeiro fim de semana, estão previstos shows de nomes como Foo Fighters, Avenged Sevenfold, Calvin Harris e Elton John, além de dezenas de outras atrações.

A previsão do tempo, no entanto, pode sofrer alterações até os dias do festival.

O primeiro dia do Rock in Rio, na sexta-feira (4), deve ser o mais quente do feriadão.

A previsão indica mínima de 18°C e máxima de 30°C , sem chuva . O dia deve começar com sol e diminuição de nuvens pela manhã, seguido de uma tarde ensolarada e uma noite com poucas nuvens.

A umidade do ar deve variar entre 50% e 89%. Os ventos serão fracos, com velocidade prevista de 4 km/h e rajadas de até 28 km/h.

No Palco Mundo, o destaque da noite é o Foo Fighters, que tem show marcado para 0h05. Antes da banda americana, sobem ao palco Nova Twins, The Hives e Rise Against.

Dave Grohl, vocalista do Foo Fighters, no Rock in Rio 2019 — Foto: Marcelo Brandt/G1

No sábado (5), a temperatura cai bastante. A previsão aponta mínima de 20°C e máxima de 23°C , com sensação térmica entre 20°C e 21°C.

O Climatempo prevê 7,2 mm de chuva e 85% de possibilidade de precipitação . A previsão é de sol entre algumas nuvens, mas com chuva rápida durante o dia e também à noite.

A umidade deve ficar elevada, entre 79% e 93%.

É o dia de atrações como Sepultura, MGK, Bring Me The Horizon e Avenged Sevenfold no Palco Mundo. O show da banda americana Avenged Sevenfold está previsto para 0h05.

Rock in Rio tem dia mais metal com Sepultura, Avenged Sevenfold, Bring Me The Horizon e mais — Foto: Reprodução

O domingo (6) deve ser o dia mais complicado do primeiro fim de semana do festival em relação ao tempo.

A previsão indica mínima de 16°C e máxima de apenas 19°C, com sensação térmica entre 16°C e 18°C.

Também é o dia com maior volume de chuva previsto: 16,8 mm e 84% de chance de precipitação . A previsão aponta tempo chuvoso durante o dia e à noite.

Os ventos também devem ficar mais fortes, com velocidade média de 9 km/h e rajadas de até 50 km/h.

No Palco Mundo, a programação tem Barão Vermelho Encontro Formação Original, Nelly, Black Eyed Peas e o DJ Calvin Harris, responsável pelo encerramento da noite, à 0h05.

Black Eyed Peas, Calvin Harris e Nelly se apresentam no Rock in Rio neste domingo (6) — Foto: Reprodução

Segunda-feira, feriado: frio e possibilidade de chuva

O feriado de 7 de setembro, último dia do primeiro bloco do Rock in Rio, também deve ter temperaturas baixas.

A previsão é de mínima de 15°C e máxima de 19°C, com sensação térmica entre 15°C e 17°C .

Há 80% de chance de chuva, mas o volume previsto é menor que o do domingo: 2,7 mm. O dia deve ter sol entre algumas nuvens e chuva passageira . À noite, a previsão é de tempo firme.

Os ventos devem soprar a 7 km/h, com rajadas de até 39 km/h.

O grande destaque da programação é o show de Elton John, marcado para 0h05 no Palco Mundo. Antes dele, se apresentam Luísa Sonza com Roberto Menescal, Jon Batiste e Gilberto Gil.

Gilberto Gil, Elton John e Laufey são algumas das atrações do dia 7 de setembro no Rock in Rio — Foto: Reprodução

Quem não for ao Parque Olímpico também poderá acompanhar o festival. O Rock in Rio será transmitido ao vivo pelo Multishow, pelo Canal Bis e pelo Globoplay, além de flashes e especiais na programação da TV Globo.

A transmissão pelo Multishow começa às 15h15, enquanto o Canal Bis inicia às 15h50. No sinal aberto, os cinco palcos terão transmissão alternada entre Multishow e Bis a partir das 15h30.

articles.title: Rock in Rio 2026: Cidade do Rock está pronta para receber o público | G1
articles.standfirst: O festival ocupa novamente o Parque Olímpico, na Zona Oeste do Rio, e terá quatro palcos principais, além de espaços dedicados à gastronomia, cultura e entretenimento.
articles.summary: A Cidade do Rock recebe o Rock in Rio 2026 no Parque Olímpico com 190 shows, espaços culturais e grandes nomes da música internacional em quatro palcos.
articles.body:
A Cidade do Rock está pronta para receber o público para mais uma edição do Rock in Rio. Ao longo de sete dias de festival, são previstos 190 shows, com mais de 1.300 artistas e 45 atrações internacionais. A expectativa é reunir cerca de 100 mil pessoas por dia.

O festival ocupa novamente o Parque Olímpico, na Zona Oeste do Rio, e terá quatro palcos principais, além de espaços dedicados à gastronomia, cultura e entretenimento.

Segundo Roberta Medina, vice-presidente executiva do Rock in Rio, a preparação para o festival envolveu meses de trabalho.

"Chegou a hora de viver o sonho. São meses construindo essa expectativa, cada detalhe com o público. A hora agora é de ser feliz, celebrar, cantar e dançar", afirmou.

Palco Sunset — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Um dos principais espaços do festival é o Palco Sunset, que terá quatro apresentações por dia, a partir das 15h30.

A programação reúne nomes nacionais e internacionais, com atrações como Capital Inicial, Ne-Yo, Péricles e Zara Larsson.

A organização recomenda que o público chegue cedo para aproveitar também as atrações e experiências espalhadas pela Cidade do Rock.

Global Village — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Outro destaque é o Global Village, espaço que reúne música e referências culturais de diferentes partes do mundo.

A programação inclui shows de artistas como Paulinho Moska e João Bosco, além de apresentações de balé. O espaço é formado por construções que representam diferentes lugares e culturas.

Espaço Favela — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

O Espaço Favela, que ganhou espaço nas últimas edições do festival, volta a receber artistas ligados às comunidades brasileiras.

"Esse é o nosso xodó", disse Roberta Medina durante a visita ao espaço. Segundo ela, o palco representa artistas que começaram nas comunidades e conquistaram espaço no Brasil e no exterior.

Entre as atrações estão Belo, Xamã, Tiee e Marvvila.

O Palco Mundo, principal palco do festival, também ganhou novidades nesta edição.

A estrutura terá uma grande tela de LED, com cerca de 2.400 metros quadrados. A proposta é que os recursos visuais sejam adaptados a cada apresentação, criando cenários diferentes para os artistas.

Entre os nomes que passam pelo palco estão Foo Fighters, Calvin Harris, Elton John e Maroon 5.

Quem não for à Cidade do Rock também poderá acompanhar o festival.

Os shows terão transmissão ao vivo pelo Globoplay, Multishow e BIS. Na TV Globo, haverá flashes ao longo da programação e um programa especial exibido todas as noites do festival.

articles.title: Eleições Caprichoso e Garantido: chapas buscam apoio de associados | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidatos de Caprichoso e Garantido fazem campanha em Manaus e Parintins; votação será em 13 de setembro, exclusiva para sócios.
articles.summary: Com o fim das inscrições, candidatos à presidência dos bois-bumbás iniciam campanha para a votação de 13 de setembro, restrita aos sócios em Manaus e Parintins.
articles.body:
Caprichoso e Garantido no Festival de Parintins 2026 — Foto: Secom

O prazo para inscrição das chapas que vão disputar as presidências dos bois-bumbás Caprichoso e Garantido terminou. Agora, a eleição movimenta os bastidores do Festival de Parintins , com candidatos buscando apoio entre os associados nas cidades de Parintins e Manaus .

No Caprichoso, duas chapas disputam a presidência. A primeira é liderada por Márcio Azedo, com Afrânio Gonçalves como vice. A segunda tem Diego Mascarenhas e Edwan Oliveira.

No Garantido, três chapas estão na disputa. A primeira é de Marialvo Brandão e Albano Albuquerque. A segunda reúne Rafael Júnior e Clodoaldo Batista. Já a terceira tem Ronildo Monteverde e Alan Gomes.

A eleição é considerada decisiva para o futuro dos dois bois. As novas diretorias terão a missão de conduzir as associações e preparar os grupos para os próximos desafios dentro e fora da arena.

A votação está marcada para 13 de setembro de 2026, em Manaus e Parintins. Os locais serão divulgados pelas associações. Apenas sócios podem participar: quem é associado ao Garantido vota nas chapas do Garantido, e quem é sócio do Caprichoso vota nas chapas do Caprichoso.

articles.title: Festas de Agosto confirmam Montes Claros como importante destino turístico | G1
articles.standfirst: Religiosidade, folclore e cultura atraem visitantes e filhos ausentes.
articles.summary: Religiosidade, folclore e cultura atraem visitantes e filhos ausentes.
articles.body:
“Para o ano eu voltarei pra cumprir nova missão”. A música, entoada por marujos, catopês e caboclinhos, representa bem o espírito das Festas de Agosto: uma missão secular, uma tradição viva, que invade as ruas da cidade tão logo sopram os ventos de agosto para mostrar a força da cultura montes-clarense.

Gerações se unem para manter eternas as festas centenárias — Foto: Julia Fernandes

Este ano, mais uma vez, a missão foi cumprida. Durante cinco dias, catopês, marujos e caboclinhos saíram às ruas para honrar o legado que herdaram de seus ancestrais e que seguem passando para as novas gerações. Com danças, cantos, tambores de viola e suas vestimentas, eles transformam o centro da cidade em um vibrante reduto de cores, sons e devoção, com os tradicionais cortejos que conduzem as homenagens a Nossa Senhora do Rosário, São Benedito e ao Divino Espírito Santo. A cada dia, os foliões seguiram pelas ruas em direção à Igrejinha do Rosário e à Praça da Matriz. Além dos cortejos, realizaram levantamento de mastros, em momentos de profunda espiritualidade. Em paralelo aos ritos religiosos, o Festival Folclórico, realizado na Praça da Matriz, abrigou shows musicais gratuitos, exibições de cinema, oficinas, capoeira e exposições artísticas.

A cantora norte-mineira Marina Sena voltou para celebrar a tradição: “ver os ternos, os catopês, trazendo tanta alegria e tanta benção, é maravilhoso” — Foto: Silvana Mameluque

Os dois eventos, a cidade vestida de fitas, a herança secular, a história viva nas ruas, tudo isso atrai visitantes de várias regiões de Minas Gerais, do Brasil e até mesmo do exterior, além, claro, dos montes-clarenses ausentes, que chegam à cidade para matar saudades e para viver o evento que remete à infância, tem um grande valor sentimental e é motivo de muito orgulho. Dentre os muitos visitantes que retornaram à cidade para vivenciar as Festas esteve a cantora norte-mineira Marina Sena. Ela fez questão de desfilar nos cortejos e participar do levantamento de mastros: "estar na cidade, participar das Festas, ver os ternos, os catopês, trazendo tanta alegria e tanta benção, é maravilhoso. O que eles fazem aqui todo ano é muito lindo. Eles são o foco de tudo. São a verdadeira beleza da Festa”.

“É bom pra todo mundo”, afirma a artista plástica Fernanda Lima, que vendeu suas peças durante as Festas — Foto: Andrey Godinho

A Festa para muitos é quando a cidade se veste completamente de cultura, com as pessoas mais voltadas para as suas raízes, para o que é produzido pelos fazedores de arte da cidade. É assim para Fernanda Lima, artista plástica que estava com suas peças à venda na lojinha de souvenirs do Centro de Atendimento ao Turista (CAT), que funcionou durante as Festas no Sobrado Versiani-Maurício. “As Festas de Agosto transformam a cidade em arte. As ruas ficam coloridas, fica tudo muito mais bonito. As pessoas voltam o olhar para a arte, querem comprar uma lembrança para levar para a cidade onde moram, para dar de presente, se interessam mais pelo artesanato. Eu, como artista plástica, percebo isso. Outro ponto é que nas Festas de Agosto a gente fica mais inspirado e produz mais. É bom pra todo mundo!”, avalia ela.

Para o setor de serviços e para o turismo, o período é um dos mais lucrativos e dinâmicos do ano para Montes Claros. O evento, que atrai muitos turistas, promove a consolidação da cidade no mapa do turismo cultural e religioso, movimentando a economia, já que aumenta a ocupação de hotéis e pousadas. Bares e restaurantes registram altas taxas de ocupação e consumo.

Luiz Fernando, de Belo Horizonte, não poupou elogios: “impressionantes a beleza, a riqueza, a alegria da festa” — Foto: Andrey Godinho

Visitando a cidade e participando das Festas pela primeira vez, Luiz Fernando, que é de Belo Horizonte, não poupou elogios. “Impressionantes a beleza, a riqueza, a alegria da festa, que completa 185 anos, e também do Festival, com seus 46 anos. Tive a oportunidade de acompanhar marujos, catopês e caboclinhos. É muito interessante. É uma festa muito colorida e que tem a participação da população, dos artistas da cidade e uma estrutura muito legal para receber os turistas”, ressaltou ele, afirmando que pretende voltar à cidade para mais festas.

Com quase 200 anos, as Festas de Agosto marcam a identidade da cidade, da sua gente, e vão muito além: elas são patrimônio, memória e valorização do passado, e também são o presente. O Festival Folclórico, com seu quase meio século, soma-se às Festas, trazendo para as ruas as vozes dos artistas locais, a arte em suas mais diversas expressões e tudo mais que remete às raízes do Arraial, agora transformado em cidade.

articles.summary: Duane “Keffe D" Davis became the first person convicted in the rap icon’s 1996 drive-by shooting death after jurors deliberated for about three hours.
articles.body: A Nevada jury on Monday found Duane "Keffe D" Davis guilty of first-degree murder with the use of a deadly weapon in the 1996 drive-by shooting death of rap icon Tupac Shakur. Davis, 63, could face life in prison after becoming the first person convicted in the nearly 30-year-old case, according to The Associated Press. Jurors deliberated for about three hours following closing arguments in the closely watched trial. Shakur’s sister, Sekyiwa "Set" Shakur, cried after the verdict was read, while Davis’ son covered his face with one hand.TUPAC MURDER TRIAL FACES ‘SNITCHES GET STITCHES’ PROBLEM BUT DEFENDANT'S GHOSTWRITER COULD BE KEY In closing arguments, Prosecutor Binu Palal said Davis obtained a gun and "went hunting" for Shakur and Marion "Suge" Knight after they attacked Davis' nephew, according to The Associated Press. He said Davis consistently placed himself inside the Cadillac used in the shooting. TUPAC SHAKUR MURDER TRIAL'S FIRST WEEK HAD HEATED TESTIMONY FROM RELUCTANT WITNESSES WITH OLD GANGLAND TIES Meanwhile, defense attorney Michael Sanft argued that no evidence beyond Davis’ statements placed him in Las Vegas or inside the car. The 16-member panel, including four alternates, heard nine days of testimony from 24 prosecution witnesses and three defense witnesses. Davis was ordered held without bail pending sentencing, which is scheduled for Oct. 13. articles.summary: A jury convicts Duane 'Keffe D' Davis of first-degree murder in orchestrating the 1996 killing of rap icon Tupac Shakur.The verdict comes nearly 30 ye.
articles.body: A jury convicts Duane 'Keffe D' Davis of first-degree murder in orchestrating the 1996 killing of rap icon Tupac Shakur.The verdict comes nearly 30 years after Shakur was fatally shot in a drive-by shooting near the Las Vegas Strip. Davis was convicted after a trial that featured nine days of testimony from detectives, former gang associates and documentarians who revisited the circumstances surrounding the rapper’s death.Jury convicts Duane Davis of first-degree murderAs per reports, Davis is the only person to have been charged in Shakur’s killing. He now faces the possibility of life in prison.About Tupac death caseDavis, 63, was accused of orchestrating the killing of Shakur on Sept. 7, 1996. Davis pleaded not guilty to murder with a deadly weapon with the intent to promote, further or assist a criminal gang in the rapper’s death. He is on trial in Las Vegas, where the killing took place, and could get life in prison.The night of his murder, Shakur was in a BMW with music mogul Marion “Suge” Knight when a white Cadillac pulled up at a red light. Shakur was shot multiple times and died six days later, while Knight survived.The confrontation was rooted in a long-running feud between the Mob Piru Bloods, a gang Shakur and Knight were affiliated with, and the South Side Compton Crips, for whom Davis was a prominent leader. The case went cold until recent years, when interviews Davis gave and his 2019 tell-all memoir revived it.Prosecutor says Davis has admitted responsibilityDuring closing arguments, Chief Deputy District Attorney Binu Palal told jurors to find Davis guilty, arguing that he had repeatedly admitted responsibility for Shakur’s murder. Palal pointed to four statements made by Davis that prosecutors relied on during the trial: a 2008 proffer interview with federal law enforcement, a 2009 interview with Las Vegas police, a 2017 Death Row Chronicles interview and Davis’ 2019 memoir, Compton Street Legend.Prosecutor shows jurors book excerptsAs reported by AP, prosecutors also presented excerpts from the memoir, including the line: “Them jumping on my nephew gave us the ultimate green light to do something to their asses.”Palal rejected the defence argument that Davis had been lying about his involvement, telling jurors that no witness had testified that he was lying. He also cited former detective Daryn Dupree’s testimony that he believed Davis was telling the truth because he would not have implicated his own nephew in the shooting if his account were fabricated.Prosecutor says Davis benefited from telling the truthAccording to Palal, Davis had an incentive to be truthful during his 2008 proffer interview, which was conducted as part of an agreement that could have helped him avoid a life sentence. The prosecutor also argued that he repeatedly corrected investigators when they presented information he believed was inaccurate.Palal told jurors that Davis’ statements were inconsistent with someone attempting to fabricate a story, arguing that he could have portrayed himself merely as a witness rather than making statements that could expose him to criminal liability for the murder.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.body: 'Toxic' actor Akshay Oberoi and his wife, Jyothi Vynatheya, have created a peaceful second home amid the lush landscape of Karjat, Maharashtra. Far removed from the pace of city life, the property is envisioned as a place where the family can slow down, spend time together and gradually build a home filled with personal memories. According to Architectural Digest, Oberoi and Jyothi entrusted interior designer and architect Nishita Kamdar with shaping the interiors of their dreamy Karjat retreat. The family visits the property around twice a month, allowing the home to evolve gradually rather than being completed all at once.Inside Akshay Oberoi and Jyothi Vynatheya’s serene Karjat homeThe Karjat property is surrounded by greenery and designed to embrace its natural setting. One of its defining features is an open courtyard that allows the outdoors to become an extension of the home. The residence also enjoys quiet, expansive views of the surrounding landscape, giving the family a much-needed escape from Mumbai's constant energy. Rather than creating an overly formal holiday home, the idea appears to be centred on warmth, comfort and a strong connection with nature. As the publication has reported, the home is coming together in what can best be described as poetic chapters, with its rooms and corners slowly acquiring more personality through the things the family loves.Books, puzzles, vinyl and Lego sculptures fill Akshay Oberoi's home with personal memoriesThe interiors are being shaped not only by design decisions but also by the Oberoi family's everyday interests and memories. Shelves around the house are gradually being filled with puzzles, books and Akshay's personal vinyl collection. The home also features Lego sculptures created by Akshay and his son Aviyaan, turning family time into a part of the property's décor.The walls, too, are expected to acquire a more personal identity over time. The family plans to decorate them with works by homegrown artists, bringing Indian art into the retreat while continuing to add to the home's evolving visual character. The result is a space that feels intentionally unfinished in the best possible way, with room for memories, objects and artwork to accumulate naturally over the years.An open courtyard and sleepy views connect Akshay Oberoi's Karjat retreat to natureNature is clearly central to the way Akshay and Jyothi envision their second home. The open courtyard and the property's peaceful views allow the landscape to remain an important part of the experience rather than simply serving as a backdrop. Oberoi is also an avid gardener and has bigger plans for the land surrounding the house. The actor hopes to introduce sustainable systems, including rainwater harvesting and drip irrigation.The land is also expected to be tilled, with mango and jackfruit trees among the additions planned for the property. The actor has even imagined creating a small, quiet spot beside a stream.“It would be nice to build a little bench to sit by the stream too,” he said.Akshay Oberoi plans a greener and more sustainable Karjat homeThe family's vision for the Karjat property extends beyond interiors and architecture. Their plans for rainwater harvesting, drip irrigation and planting fruit trees suggest a long-term effort to develop the land while remaining closely connected to its natural environment. Mango and jackfruit trees could eventually add another layer of character to the retreat, while the proposed bench by the stream captures the slower rhythm the family appears to be seeking at the property. For a home visited only a couple of times each month, the Karjat retreat is gradually becoming a deeply personal family space. Each visit appears to add another object, memory or idea to the home, allowing it to grow organically alongside the family.Akshay Oberoi’s Karjat retreat is a home that is still evolvingWhat makes Akshay Oberoi and Jyothi Vynatheya's Karjat home particularly distinctive is that it is not being treated as a finished design project. Instead, the family is allowing the home to take shape gradually, with books, puzzles, vinyl records, Lego creations and future artworks becoming part of its story over time. With its open courtyard, sleepy green views and plans for a flourishing garden, the property reflects a desire to create a retreat where nature and family life coexist. The home's design by Nishita Kamdar provides the framework for that vision, while the Oberoi family continues to add its own personality, one chapter at a time.Akshay Oberoi was last seen in ‘Toxic’On the work front, Akshay Oberoi was last seen in 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups', starring Yash, Nayanthara, Rukmini Vasanth, Huma Qureshi, Kiara Advani, Sanjeeda Sheikh and Tara Sutaria. articles.title: Sandra Bullock Recalls First ‘Practical Magic’ Bombing After Thinking ‘People Are Going to Love It’: ‘And Then It Got Quiet’
articles.summary: The Owen sisters may be back in “Practical Magic 2” 28 years after Nicole Kidman and Sandra Bullock first played the sibling witches, but that doesn’t mean t...
articles.body:
The Owen sisters may be back in "Practical Magic 2" 28 years after Nicole Kidman and Sandra Bullock first played the sibling witches, but that doesn't mean the first movie's outing doesn't still sting a little.

The original "Practical Magic" was a critical and box office failure before earning cult classic status over the last almost three decades.

"We thought, 'This is going to be such an amazing film. People are going to love it,'" Bullock recalled. "And then it got quiet. It got quiet. [They] were like, 'How many women in a film do you need? How many tones do you need? What kind of film is this?'

"And here's the thing that I really wanna bring up and I bring it up ad nauseum, Griffin Dunne created this world with us," Bullock said, referring to the first film's director.

Kidman added, "And he loved us and he let us shine."

Bullock continued, "It's because of him, this film exists and he never got to smell the flowers when we made it. So tonight we're honoring him."

Why did they decide to make the sequel now?

"It just happened," Kidman said. It was more like serendipity and it came and we were ready and everything fell into place. It's like in life — you try to force things, it doesn't work. You have to wait, be patient, and we both kind of open to it."

"Practical Magic 2" is based on Alice Hoffman's novel "The Book of Magic." Directed by Susanne Bier, the film sees the return of original stars Kidman, Bullock, Stockard Channing and Dianne Wiest. Newcomers include Joey King, Maisie Williams, Lee Pace, Xolo Maridueña and Solly McLeod.

This is the second time King worked with Kidman following the 2024 rom-com "Family Affair" with Zac Efron. "When you have someone who has been through so much, who is open and loving with their knowledge, I couldn't be more grateful," King told me of her relationship with Kidman. "I feel so lucky to be able to go to her."

articles.body: Actress Revathy has emphasised that ensuring women’s safety in society requires more than asking women to be cautious about their surroundings. Speaking at the 6th Bharat Soka GSSI Women’s Awareness Seminar in Chennai, the actor highlighted the importance of raising boys with an understanding of respect, responsibility and the difference between right and wrong.The seminar was held at the Music Academy in Chennai on Sunday under the theme “Women in the Century: Awareness and Action.” It brought together women from different generations, including senior citizens and young girls, who spoke about personal struggles and how they transformed those challenges into achievements.Revathy on raising boys the right wayWhile speaking to reporters at the event, as quoted by ANI, Revathy said conversations around women’s safety often place the responsibility on women themselves. She stressed that greater attention needs to be paid to what boys learn at home, in schools and in wider society.“On one hand, women are advised to be mindful of their safety, including where they should and should not go. But what is much more important is how we raise boys. We need to pay attention to what boys see and learn as they grow up at home, in schools and in society. Only by teaching them to clearly understand what is right and what is wrong can we bring about major changes in society,” said Revathy.Her comments focused on the need for a broader social approach to women’s safety, with families and educational institutions playing an important role in shaping how young boys understand behaviour, boundaries and respect.Revathy highlights growing opportunities for womenRevathy also spoke about the increasing opportunities available to women across different fields, including the film industry. According to the actor, women today have greater access to opportunities, but their progress also depends on how they use those opportunities and build on their individual talents and abilities. Her remarks come at a time when conversations around women’s participation and representation across professional fields continue to evolve, with younger generations increasingly entering spaces that were less accessible to women in the past.Revathy expresses confidence in Gen ZThe actor also expressed optimism about the present generation and said she believes Gen Z has the potential to accomplish things that previous generations could not.“I have a great deal of confidence that the present Gen Z generation will achieve and accomplish many things that our generation was unable to,” she said.Revathy on the work frontHaving debuted in 'Love' opposite Salman Khan, the duo reunited in 'Tiger 3' where she was seen as Maithili Menon. articles.summary: La actriz revela los detalles de su preparación en una entrevista concedida a Empire
articles.body: La saga de videojuegos 'Street Fighter' presentan a Chun-Li como una de las mujeres más fuertes del mundo. Sus patadas son legendarias y la potencia en sus piernas está fuera de toda duda. La actriz canadiense Callina Liang era consciente de que debía estar a la altura que interpreta en la próxima película 'Street Fighter' y se ha sometido a una preparación muy exigente. "Hicimos un montón de entrenamiento de Taekwondo, Muay Thai y Wushu. Entrenaba dos horas al día, lo que me ayudó a fortalecer mucho las piernas y a cambiar drásticamente mi dieta", explicó en la revista Empire. La alimentación de la artista es otro de los elementos que más ha llamado la atención de sus declaraciones. "Cuando estaba en fase de volumen, comía 12 huevos al día. Tenía que comer cada dos horas y estaba a punto de vomitar", se sinceró en la conversación con el citado medio. El esfuerzo, afortunadamente, valió la pena y su cuerpo se acercó más al de Chun-Li. "Pero funcionó. Al final del rodaje, mis muslos habían crecido seis centímetros y medio cada uno", comentó. Callina Liang se ha tomado muy en serio la preparación de su personaje. De hecho, la actriz ha desvelado que ha prestado mucha atención a los movimientos de Chun-Li en los videojuegos para imitarlos a la perfección. La nueva entrega de la película 'Street Fighter' parece ser una de las versiones más fieles a los videojuegos, hábitat en que el nació la saga, y la canadiense no tiene ninguna intención de decepcionar a sus seguidores. La nueva película 'Street Fighter' llegará a los cines de España el próximo 16 de octubre. Dirigida por Kitao Sakurai, está interpretada por Andrew Koji (Ryu), Noah Centineo (Ken), Callina Liang (Chun-Li), Cody Rhodes (Guile), Vidyut Jammwal (Dhalsim), David Dastmalchian (Bison), 50 Cent (Balrog), Jason Momoa (Blanka), Hirooki Goto (Honda), Mel Jarnson (Cammy), Roman Reigns (Akuma) y Orville Peck (Vega).

articles.body: Yash-starrer ‘Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups’ is maintaining its theatrical momentum as it enters its seventh day at the box office. The immediate domestic target now is the Rs. 225 crore India net mark, followed by the Rs. 250 crore milestone. With the film already at Rs. 221.91 crore on Day 7 live tracking, it needs roughly Rs 28 crore more to reach the first milestone. The next major worldwide benchmark could be Rs. 310 crore. Having crossed Rs. 300 crore globally after six days, the film has already established a strong international footprint.Toxic Movie Review'Toxic' Day 1 to Day 6 earnings‘Toxic’ opened with Rs. 101.10 crore net on Day 1, setting the tone for its theatrical run. The film collected Rs. 37.65 crore on Day 2, followed by Rs. 27.20 crore on Day 3. It then added Rs. 25.15 crore on Day 4 and Rs. 23 crore on Day 5. The first five days took its India net collection to Rs. 214.10 crore. On Day 6, ‘Toxic’ collected Rs 7.45 crore net in India, a 67.6% decline from its Day 5 collection.The film’s international performance also contributed significantly to its early worldwide total. It opened with Rs. 20 crore overseas on Day 1, followed by Rs. 8 crore on Day 2 and Rs. 3.50 crore on Day 3. By the end of Day 5, the overseas gross had reached Rs 29.25 crore. The overseas market contributed another Rs. 2 crore on Day 6, taking the international gross to Rs. 39.25 crore. By the end of Day 6, the film had reached Rs. 221.55 crore India net and Rs. 304.05 crore worldwide gross.'Toxic' Day 7 collection live trackingAccording to Sacnilk's live tracking, ‘Toxic’ has added Rs. 2.96 crore net to its domestic collection across 7,554 shows.With the day's final business yet to be reported, the film's domestic net total has reached Rs 224.71 crore, while the India now gross stands at Rs 268.49 crore.The latest language-wise live figures include Rs. 1.89 crore from Hindi, Rs. 69 lakh from Kannada, Rs. 26 lakh from Telugu and Rs. 12 lakh from Tamil.Day wise collections for 'Toxic'Day 1: Rs. 101.10 croreDay 2: Rs. 37.65 croreDay 3: Rs. 27.20 croreDay 4: Rs. 25.15 croreDay 5: Rs. 23.00 croreDay 6: Rs. 7.45 croreDay 7 [LIVE]: Rs. 2.96 croreTOTAL: Rs. 224.71 croreMore about 'Toxic'Directed by Geetu Mohandas, ‘Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups’ is a gangster drama set against the backdrop of Portuguese-era Goa. articles.body: With the release of 'Ramayana' Part 1 drawing closer, anticipation surrounding Nitesh Tiwari’s ambitious adaptation of the epic continues to build. The film’s trailer, released on July 30, offered audiences a first look at Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Yash as Ravana, Sai Pallavi as Sita and several other key characters. However, one major cast member was notably absent from the trailer, Sunny Deol, who plays Lord Hanuman.Now, according to a report by Bollywood Hungama, the makers may be deliberately keeping Sunny’s appearance under wraps until the very end of the first instalment, potentially setting up a major cliffhanger for 'Ramayana' Part 2.Sunny Deol’s Lord Hanuman reveal reportedly saved for the endAccording to the report, Sunny Deol will appear only towards the conclusion of Ramayana Part 1. His introduction could reportedly be positioned as the film’s final scene or even as a mid-credit or post-credit sequence. The reported strategy appears designed to generate maximum curiosity around the character and create a theatrical moment that leaves audiences wanting more. A source cited by Bollywood Hungama reportedly compared the approach to the ending of 'Baahubali: The Beginning', where the question surrounding Kattappa and Baahubali became a major pop-culture talking point ahead of the sequel.If the report is accurate, the introduction of Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman could similarly become the big talking point after 'Ramayana' Part 1 ends.Why 'Ramayana' makers may be keeping Sunny Deol’s Hanuman look under wrapsSunny Deol’s absence from the promotional material so far has naturally generated considerable curiosity. While Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, Sai Pallavi, Rakul Preet Singh and other members of the ensemble have featured prominently in the trailer and promotional campaign, Sunny’s portrayal of Lord Hanuman remains largely unseen by the general audience. The decision could be particularly significant given the scale of the project and the expectations surrounding Sunny’s casting. Rather than revealing his look in advance, the makers may be attempting to preserve the character’s first appearance as a big-screen reveal. Interestingly, a select group of industry attendees had already received a glimpse of Sunny Deol as Hanuman during an exclusive presentation of Ramayana footage at CinemaCon 2026 in Las Vegas earlier this year. According to reports at the time, the footage showed the actor in an entirely different avatar.15-minute ‘Ramayana’ footage impresses exhibitors at Big Cine Expo 2026The buzz around Ramayana received another boost following the screening of approximately 15 minutes of previously unreleased footage at Big Cine Expo 2026 in Chennai. The two-day exhibition event was held on August 18 and 19, with the exclusive Ramayana presentation taking place on the first day. The footage had not been made available to the public, and exhibitors were reportedly prohibited from recording the presentation.According to the same publication's earlier report, an exhibitor who attended the screening, the presentation featured several previously unseen creatures, including a one-eyed daitya and a bear-like creature. articles.title: Meghan Markle’s UK return poses Palace control ‘nightmare,’ expert warns
articles.summary: Meghan Markle's U.K. return means Buckingham Palace can't control her projects, but experts say the institution still holds leverage over royal access.
articles.body: Meghan Markle is returning to Britain with more independence than she had as a working royal, an arrangement experts say could test Buckingham Palace's boundaries. Markle, 45, and Prince Harry, 41, recently relocated to the United Kingdom with their children Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, for an extended stay though they will remain private, non-working members of the royal family. While the couple is expected to establish a private residence outside London and keep their home in Montecito, California, royal observers told Fox News Digital that Markle's ability to pursue her own media, business and public-facing projects from Britain could create new tension with the institution she once represented. PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE PLANNING TO MOVE BACK TO UK WITH CHILDREN 6 YEARS AFTER ROYAL EXIT: REPORTS "The nightmare for the Palace is that they can’t be controlled," royal commentator Richard Fitzwilliams told Fox News Digital. "Diary clashes will probably mean royal engagements are overshadowed by what the Sussexes choose to do and what they are, or are not, asked to by the Palace." Kinsey Schofield, host of YouTube’s "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered," said that Buckingham Palace will have "very little control" over the Duke and Duchess of Sussex's public and commercial activities because they no longer represent Harry's father King Charles as working royals. PRINCE HARRY'S MOST CONTROVERSIAL ROYAL PLAN COULD STILL BECOME REALITY, AUTHOR SAYS "They are private citizens and no longer working on behalf of the King, so Buckingham Palace isn’t approving Meghan’s interviews, appearances, Instagram posts or commercial projects," Schofield said. "But Harry is still the King’s son and Meghan is still the Duchess of Sussex, so there is an inevitable association with the monarchy," she added. "That’s the complicated part. They can operate independently while still benefiting from an enormous amount of public interest that exists because of Harry’s DNA." MEGHAN MARKLE’S ROYAL EXIT HAD WARNING SIGNS YEARS EARLIER, VETERAN CORRESPONDENT REVEALS Markle's status as a private citizen living in the U.K. marks a sharp departure from her life as a working royal, when Palace protocols and communications staff shaped much of her public role. The former "Suits" star is returning with her own career, team and support system, according to People magazine. "She has been vocal about how she felt about it before, but that doesn’t mean things are going to be exactly the same again," an ally told People. "It doesn’t mean it can’t be different and can’t change." Another source told the outlet that the Sussexes' support network is "stronger now than it ever was to protect her — to protect them." However, Schofield pointed out that Buckingham Palace retains one important source of influence. KING CHARLES SENDS 'DEFIANCE' MESSAGE TO PRINCE WILLIAM WITH BUCKINGHAM PALACE ROOM OFFER TO HARRY: EXPERT "The palace can’t control what they do, but it can control access to the institution. It can decide how much proximity they have to working royals, royal residences, and official events," she said. "That is where the palace still has considerable leverage." "Meghan may be returning without palace restrictions, but she is also returning without palace protection," she added. "You don’t get one without losing the other." PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE BLASTED FOR ‘FAUX ROYAL TOUR’ AS EXPERTS ACCUSE COUPLE OF EXPLOITING TITLES However, Buckingham Palace's ability to limit the Sussexes’ access to official royal events, however, would not prevent their public appearances, announcements or business ventures from drawing attention away from the working royals. Fitzwilliams said that dynamic could become particularly challenging when it comes to the carefully coordinated royal calendar. "The problem is that royal diaries are planned well in advance," Fitzwilliams said. "Here there are likely to be numerous clashes, and this will fuel fascination with the Sussexes." PRINCE WILLIAM LIKELY 'LIVID' OVER MEGHAN MARKLE'S 'TASTELESS' PHOTOS AT PRINCESS DIANA'S HOME: EXPERT Schofield told Fox News Digital that a competing announcement would not necessarily violate a formal Palace rule, but she noted there are longstanding expectations around the timing of public engagements. "If Meghan were repeatedly scheduling appearances or announcements to coincide with major royal engagements, people would notice," she said. "She might not be breaking a written rule, but there are conventions and courtesies around these things." PRINCE WILLIAM'S ABSENCE SPEAKS VOLUMES AS KING CHARLES REUNITES WITH PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE: EXPERTS "If you consistently attempt to overshadow the working Royal Family, eventually the pattern becomes the story," Schofield added. Schofield explained that the concern over competing headlines echoes the central issue Queen Elizabeth II confronted when Harry and Markle stepped back from their roles as working royals in 2020. At the time, the late queen rejected a proposed hybrid arrangement that would have allowed the couple to pursue financial independence while continuing to carry out official duties and retain the benefits of their royal connection. "This is essentially the dilemma the late Queen was trying to avoid with the original ‘half-in, half-out’ rejection," Schofield said. "Meghan can enjoy enormous interest because she married into the Royal Family without having to behave or work like a royal." "But there is another side to that bargain," she continued. "She doesn’t have the institution behind her anymore either. There is no royal communications operation required to defend her, no royal security, and no guaranteed place at major royal occasions. A lot of the perks are gone." The experts agreed that the question of access is further complicated by the fractured relationship between the Sussexes and the royal family. The couple publicly detailed strains within the royal family in their 2021 interview with Oprah Winfrey, their 2022 Netflix docuseries "Harry & Meghan" and Harry’s bombshell 2023 memoir "Spare." Schofield said that history could make Palace staff particularly wary as Harry and Markle establish a new life in the U.K. "There is also a significant trust deficit," she said. "Harry published private family conversations in ‘Spare,’ and Harry and Meghan have discussed private royal relationships publicly in interviews and their Netflix series. That history doesn’t disappear simply because they’re living in Britain again." British broadcaster Helena Chard told Fox News Digital that Charles and his son and heir Prince William may need to establish clearer expectations around the Sussexes’ access to official engagements and the working royal family as they settle back into Britain. "Formalities need to be drawn up, put in place and made clear to all," Chard said. "These will essentially be the 'dos and don'ts' formalities." According to People magazine, the Sussexes' move back to the U.K. is also about more than their business interests or public profiles. The outlet reported that the decision was "taken as a family," with the couple viewing a longer stay in Britain as an opportunity to connect their children with Harry’s heritage. Earlier this summer, Archie and Lilibet joined their parents for a trip to the U.K. during which they reunited with Charles and Queen Camilla at Highgrove House, the king's country home. The children also visited Althorp, the childhood home and final resting place of Harry's late mother, Princess Diana. They were joined by Harry's uncle and Diana's brother Charles Spencer, and members of the late Princess of Wales' family. Another insider shared that Harry wants his children "to understand the world he grew up in and where their family comes from." Meanwhile, not every royal observer expects Markle’s return to immediately deepen the rift. articles.title: Quote of the day by Tobey Maguire: ‘I’m not into sugar for kids, but you don’t want your kid to be the carrot kid… You’ve got to let them eat a little cake,' the iconic actor’s lessons on parenting, nutrition, and finding the perfect balance in life
articles.summary: Tobey Maguire is best known for his beloved role as the neighborhood-friendly Spider-Man; however, beyond his career in the industry, Maguire is known.
articles.body: Tobey Maguire is best known for his beloved role as the neighborhood-friendly Spider-Man; however, beyond his career in the industry, Maguire is known to be a loving and doting father. The actor shares two children with ex-wife Jennifer Meyer: Ruby Sweetheart Maguire, who is 19 years old, and Otis Tobias Maguire, who is 17 years old. Today’s quote is all about understanding that one of the main aspects of parenting comes from understanding that your children need to lead a balanced life, and restricting them from things will not help them in the long run.The quote of the day from the beloved ‘Spider-Man’ star reads, "I'm not into sugar for kids, but you don’t want your kid to be the carrot kid. There’s always the kid at the birthday parties carrying a bag of carrots. You’ve got to let them eat a little cake.”What does the quote of the day mean?The actor shared these words during one of his appearances on ‘The Ellen DeGeneres Show’ in 2010. At the time, the actor was discussing his parenting style and his approach to raising his children with his then-wife, Jennifer Meyer.Essentially, his quote is all about understanding the concept of moderation over strict restriction in parenting, specifically navigating the balance between promoting health and preserving a child's social inclusion. The quote is about nutrition and a healthy lifestyle, which can be balanced alongside giving in to cravings every once in a while. He shared that there is no point in forcing a child to live their life a certain way all the time if you are not giving them a little leeway and teaching them about the concept of moderation.As for the social aspect of it, Maguire mentioned the phrase “carrot kid," referring to those visibly socially isolated due to their parents' overly strict rules. Taking birthday parties as an example, the actor connected this to having a balanced lifestyle for your child since such parties are one of the major places where children let go and have more fun.At the end of the day, there is no true definition of being a good parent. However, you are the only one who knows what is best for your child, though it is important to understand that everything needs to be done in moderation. Whether it is helping them adopt a healthier lifestyle or understanding that some things are not meant for them all the time, it is all about leading a balanced life.About Tobey Maguire’s early life and entry into the Hollywood industryTobey Maguire was born on June 27, 1975, in Santa Monica, California. Maguire moved around a lot when he was a child and grew up in a working-class household. His parents were young and weren’t even married at the time he was born. They later separated when he was around two or three years old. His mother, Wendy Brown, used to work as a screenwriter and producer, while his father, Vincent Maguire, used to work as a cook.When he was a child, he wanted to become a chef like his father. However, when he was in sixth grade, he wanted to take home economics. However, his mother, who wanted him to go into acting, paid him USD 100 to opt for drama class, and the rest is history. The actor discovered that he had a knack for performing on stage and started taking his career in acting more seriously. After relocating again around his freshman year, he dropped out of high school altogether to pursue acting full-time.He debuted as an actor when he was 14 years old and starred in multiple roles in TV series like ‘Great Scott!’, ‘Walker, Texas Ranger,' 'Roseanne,' and ‘Blossom.’ Some of his other roles included his work in 'Parenthood,' ‘This Boy's Life,' ‘The Ice Storm,' ‘The Cider House Rules,' ‘Wonder Boys,' ‘Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas,' and many others. His big breakthrough came in 2002 when he was cast in Sam Raimi’s 'Spider-Man.' He portrayed the role until 2007 over the course of three films. Celebrity Net Worth revealed that Maguire was paid USD 4 million for the first film, along with USD 17.5 million for the second film, and a 5% backend earning from the film’s box office. Lastly, he earned a USD 15 million salary along with 7.5% of the box office.Maguire last reprised his role as ‘Spider-Man’ along with Tom Holland and Andrew Garfield in ‘Spider-Man: No Way Home’ (2021).Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Akshay Oberoi opens up on Toxic's online leak, urges fans to watch it in theatres: 'I feel immensely bad for the producer'
articles.summary: Yash's ‘Toxic’ reportedly found its way online mere hours after its theatrical debut, triggering concerns over piracy. Addressing the leak, Akshay Obe.
articles.body: Yash's ‘Toxic’ reportedly found its way online mere hours after its theatrical debut, triggering concerns over piracy. Addressing the leak, Akshay Oberoi, who plays Tony in the film, chose to take a more optimistic view of the situation. He highlighted that, unlike other films that leak online prior to their release, ‘Toxic’ managed to remain secure right up until it hit the big screen.Akshay Oberoi says he wasn't aware of the leak initiallyIn a conversation with Bollywood Bubble, Akshay said, “Some films have been leaked even before they hit the screens. But at least it only leaked post coming out in the cinema.” He admitted he wasn't aware of the leak when it first happened and further spoke about how disheartening it can be for a film to leak before it even releases in theatres.Akshay Oberoi on how devastating pre-release leaks can beAkshay pointed out that films can sometimes fall prey to leaks even before their theatrical run begins, he said, "I mean like there have been stories that are just so terrifying that, you know, like data, a disk, a hard disk leaked from some studio and now the thing is out even before it hits the cinema.” He went on to express sympathy for everyone associated with a film's making. He admitted, “immensely bad for the producer, the actors and so many people who put so much hard work.” However, he added, “Thank God, that didn’t happen with us.”Akshay Oberoi reveals why ‘Toxic’ team avoided interviews before releaseThe actor also shed light on why filmmakers and actors often keep details about their projects under wraps ahead of release, citing piracy as a major concern. He revealed that the ‘Toxic’ team made a conscious effort to avoid disclosing anything about the film's plot during its promotional run. “That’s also why everyone is so fiercely protective. Like we didn’t talk about the film or the story at all. If you notice, no one gave any interviews,” he said.Akshay Oberoi urges fans to watch Toxic in theatresAkshay also asked people to watch Toxic in theatres, the way it's meant to be seen, saying it shows respect for the hard work put into making the film.About ‘Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups’Directed by Geetu Mohandas and led by Yash, ‘Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups’ is a Kannada action thriller that marked the actor's comeback to the big screen following ‘KGF Chapter 2’. articles.body: Big & Rich saw firsthand how Dolly Parton put her fame aside after the 2016 Tennessee wildfires that devastated the community. During an interview with Fox News Digital, the country music duo, Big Kenny and John Rich, who recently released their protest single titled "Hello AI," recalled seeing Parton be an "extraordinary person" for her community and trying to help her neighbors. "One thing that struck me that particular day, you know, Gatlinburg had basically burned to the ground. And that's right in her backyard, where she's from," Rich began. "So, she was distraught over what was going on. In the moment of those performances, it wasn't like you were standing next to Dolly Parton, the world-famous iconic singer. You were standing next to a country girl who was trying to help out her neighbors. That was really her whole point." After devastating wildfires tore through Gatlinburg and Sevier County in November 2016, Parton rallied the country music community to help her native East Tennessee. Parton hosted the star-studded "Smoky Mountains Rise: A Benefit for the My People Fund" telethon on Dec. 13, with Big & Rich among the nearly 20 artists who performed. DOLLY PARTON'S LIFE IN HER OWN WORDS: FROM SMOKY MOUNTAINS POVERTY TO COUNTRY MUSIC IMMORTALITY The benefit ultimately raised more than $9 million for wildfire victims after the fires killed 14 people and damaged or destroyed more than 2,400 buildings, according to ABC News. The money supported Parton’s My People Fund, which provided direct financial assistance to families who lost their homes. And that's how I would describe her that day. DOLLY PARTON'S BELOVED LITERACY MISSION SEES SURGE OF SUPPORT AFTER COUNTRY ICON'S DEATH Big Kenny continued, "And every other time I've ever run into her, she's just a super sweet and kind and funny and smart and just every other kind of adjective you can use for an extraordinary human being like Dolly Parton." articles.body: Sarah Ferguson has made a career out of comebacks — and after seven months largely hidden from public view, the former Duchess of York may be preparing for another. Ferguson, 66, may be ready to step back into the spotlight, with one royal commentator describing the former Duchess of York as a "chameleon" who has repeatedly managed to reinvent herself. "Sarah Ferguson is forever the chameleon," British broadcaster and photographer Helena Chard told Fox News Digital. "She always seems to bounce back." SARAH FERGUSON IS HOPING 'TO EVAPORATE LIKE MIST' AS SHE'S SEEN FOR THE FIRST TIME IN 7 MONTHS: EXPERT "The one person who believes in Sarah is Sarah!" Chard added. One element of Ferguson's reported fresh start could be a new home in Britain. Chard said she understands Ferguson will be based in the Home Counties in a "£10,000 a month plush gated property with granny annex." But a new residence may only be part of the attempted reset. Chard said Ferguson has attracted interest from television producers and could use a documentary or interview to put forward her version of events. "Sarah has admittedly made some silly decisions. However, it's reported that she is lined up to appear in a TV documentary when settled in Britain," Chard said. "This is one of the options to put her side of the story forward, essentially a ‘Tell All’ interview. She has been bombarded with TV production offers. However, she is considering working on her own programme to retain control."
